Chapter 7 · Topic 16

Chemical structure of RNA

BiomoleculesBiomolecules and Practical ChemistryE. Nucleic acidsStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

RNA structure (ribose, A-U-G-C, usually single-stranded folding into hairpins, cloverleaf tRNA, ribosomal cores) acts where DNA archives: mRNA messages (capped, tailed, spliced), tRNA adaptors (anticodon plus CCA arms), rRNA machines (peptide-bond ribozymes), microRNA regulators, ribozyme catalysts. Uracil replaces thymine; 2-OH makes RNA degradable (short-lived messages suit regulation). Folding creates function from single strands.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Single-stranded folders acting as message, adaptor, machine.
  • Uracil for thymine; 2-OH for degradability.
Remember
  • Ribosome peptide bonds are RNA-catalysed (ribozyme).
NEET Practice MCQ
1

Uracil base occurs in

Solution: RNA swaps thymine for uracil in all its forms.
Example 1.

Q. RNA has uracil where DNA has thymine, plus ribose 2-OH. State two consequences.

  1. Uracil pairs adenine identically (no coding loss).
  2. 2-OH makes RNA degradable (short-lived messages suit regulation) while DNA persists (stable archive).
  3. Chemistry tunes lifespan: degradable actors, durable archives.

Answer: Same pairing, shorter lifespan - regulation-ready messages.

Back to Index
Index / Biomolecules and Practical Chemistry
Chapter 7 · Topic 17

Biological functions of DNA

BiomoleculesBiomolecules and Practical ChemistryE. Nucleic acidsStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

DNA functions (hereditary storage, replication fidelity, transcription templates, repair substrates, regulatory binding sites) run life information flow - genome archives (3 billion human bases), gene expression programmes development, mutation fuels evolution, fingerprinting identifies individuals, forensics convicts criminals, ancestry maps migrations. Central dogma (DNA-RNA-protein) organises all molecular biology - storage transcribes to messages translating to workers.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Store, replicate, transcribe, repair - information flow hub.
  • Fingerprinting, forensics, ancestry apply DNA identity.
Remember
  • Genome archives; transcriptome acts; proteome works.
NEET Practice MCQ
1

Hershey-Chase experiment proved DNA is the

Solution: 32P-DNA entered bacteria while 35S-protein stayed outside.
Example 1.

Q. If DNA is damaged by UV, which molecule carries the repair orders?

  1. Damage sensed; p53-class regulators transcribe repair genes.
  2. mRNA messages carry orders to ribosomes building repair enzymes.
  3. DNA archives, RNA messages, proteins execute.

Answer: mRNA - archive transcribes instructions for repair crews.

Back to Index
Index / Biomolecules and Practical Chemistry
Chapter 7 · Topic 18

Biological functions of RNA

BiomoleculesBiomolecules and Practical ChemistryE. Nucleic acidsStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

RNA functions span messaging (mRNA codons to ribosomes), adapting (tRNA anticodon-amino matches), catalysing (ribozymes splicing introns, bonding peptides), regulating (microRNA silencing, Xist coating, CRISPR guides), and genomes (retroviruses storing RNA, reverse-transcribing via RT). mRNA vaccines (COVID instructions), RNAi therapies (silencing disease genes) and CRISPR guides (programmable targeting) weaponise RNA functions medically.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Message, adapt, catalyse, regulate, store retroviral genomes.
  • mRNA vaccines, RNAi drugs, CRISPR guides apply RNA.
Remember
  • CRISPR guides are programmable RNA address labels.
NEET Practice MCQ
1

CRISPR-Cas9 guiding molecule is made of

Solution: RNA addresses target Cas9 cutting precisely.
Example 1.

Q. COVID mRNA vaccines instruct cells to make spike protein. Which biomolecule does what?

  1. mRNA (synthetic message) enters cells.
  2. Ribosomes translate it to spike antigen (protein).
  3. Immune system learns antigen without virus exposure.

Answer: Message in, antigen out, immunity without infection.

Chapter 7 · Topic 19

General introduction

BiomoleculesBiomolecules and Practical ChemistryF. HormonesStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Hormones (steroid, peptide and amino-acid-derived messengers: insulin-glucagon sugar push-pull, thyroid metabolic dial, cortisol stress manager, sex steroids developers, adrenaline emergency responder) coordinate via bloodstream to distant receptors - endocrine glands ductless, exocrine (milk, sweat) ducted. Feedback loops (negative mostly, positive LH-surge/labour rarely) hold set points. Plant hormones (auxin, GA, cytokinin, ethylene, ABA) parallel animal signalling greenly.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Bloodstream messengers coordinating distant targets.
  • Feedback (mostly negative) holds hormonal set points.
Hormone pairs
PointDetail
Insulin/glucagonSugar down/up
ThyroidMetabolic rate dial
CortisolStress manager
AdrenalineEmergency responder
NEET Practice MCQ
1

Insulin lowers blood sugar while glucagon

Solution: Pancreatic push-pull holds glucose steady.
Example 1.

Q. Adrenaline (emergency) vs insulin (meal) vs thyroxine (daily): match timescales.

  1. Adrenaline: seconds (fight-or-flight amine).
  2. Insulin: minutes-hours (meal glucose disposal).
  3. Thyroxine: days-weeks (metabolic dial setting).
  4. Chemistry sets speed: amines flash, peptides pulse, steroids persist.

Answer: Seconds, minutes, days - hormone chemistry times responses.

Principles Related to Practical Chemistry

Lassaigne tests, functional-group detection, titrimetry and salt analysis.

Principles Related to Practical ChemistryBiomolecules and Practical ChemistryChapter Introduction

Deep Dive · Lab skills that score

Practical chemistry runs Lassaigne element detection (N blue, S violet, X silver precipitates) through functional-group tests (hydroxyl ceric/Lucas/FeCl3 splits, carbonyl DNP/Tollens/iodoform splits, carboxyl bicarbonate fizz, amino carbylamine/Hinsberg/nitrous splits) into named compounds (acetanilide hydrolysis-plus-amine tests, iodoform methyl-carbonyl test) and quantitative lab work (titrimetry with acid-base standards plus indicator matching, salt-analysis group separations with confirmatory closes, enthalpy-kinetics-equilibrium-pH-chromatography experiments). Detect groups, confirm ions, titrate unknowns - practical trilogy.
NEET facts:
  • Carbylamine foul proves primary amines; Tollens mirror proves aldehydes.
  • Phenolphthalein suits basic endpoints; methyl orange suits acidic ones.
NEET Practice MCQ
1

Hinsberg reagent separates amine classes by sulphonamide

Solution: Sulphonamide acidity differences split the three classes.

Index / Biomolecules and Practical Chemistry
Chapter 8 · Topic 1

Nitrogen

Principles Related to Practical ChemistryBiomolecules and Practical ChemistryDetection of Extra ElementsStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Nitrogen detection (Lassaigne fusion to NaCN, then FeSO4 plus FeCl3 boiling: Prussian blue ferriferrocyanide precipitate) diagnoses N in amines, amides, nitro compounds, alkaloids - hydrazine-containing? no - false negatives in diazo compounds (N2 escapes on heating) and false positives with pre-existing cyanides. Blood-red (thiocyanate) instead signals N+S together. Blue means nitrogen present (with stated exceptions).
NEET Snapshot:
  • Prussian blue precipitate proves nitrogen.
  • Diazo compounds escape detection (N2 lost heating).
Remember
  • Blood-red instead means N+S together present.
NEET Practice MCQ
1

Lassaigne nitrogen test gives colour

Solution: Sodium cyanide plus iron salts make ferriferrocyanide blue.
Example 1.

Q. Lassaigne extract gives Prussian blue with FeSO4/FeCl3. What element and chemistry?

  1. Blue ferriferrocyanide proves nitrogen (as NaCN from fusion).
  2. Fe2+ plus cyanide makes ferrocyanide; Fe3+ turns it blue.
  3. Nitrogen present (unless diazo compound escaped as N2).

Answer: Nitrogen via Prussian blue complex.

Back to Index
Index / Biomolecules and Practical Chemistry
Chapter 8 · Topic 2

Sulphur

Principles Related to Practical ChemistryBiomolecules and Practical ChemistryDetection of Extra ElementsStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Sulphur detection (Lassaigne to Na2S, then sodium nitroprusside violet, or lead acetate black PbS) diagnoses thiols, sulphides, sulphonic acids - rotten-egg H2S confirms on acidifying. N+S together give blood-red thiocyanate (ferric test) instead of separate colours. Mustard gas, garlic allicin and vulcanised rubber all test positive - sulphur chemistry widespread.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Violet nitroprusside or black lead sulphide proves sulphur.
  • N+S together turn blood-red instead.
Remember
  • Acidify sulphide salts releases rotten-egg H2S.
NEET Practice MCQ
1

Sulphur detection by nitroprusside gives colour

Solution: Sulphide-nitroprusside complex colours violet.
Example 1.

Q. Nitroprusside turns violet with an extract; acidifying another part smells rotten eggs. Element?

  1. Violet complex proves sulphide (sulphur present).
  2. Rotten-egg H2S on acidifying confirms sulphur independently.
  3. Double confirmation: nitroprusside plus H2S smell.

Answer: Sulphur - violet test plus rotten-egg corroboration.

Chapter 8 · Topic 3

Halogens

Principles Related to Practical ChemistryBiomolecules and Practical ChemistryDetection of Extra ElementsStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Halogen detection (Lassaigne to NaX, then AgNO3: white AgCl soluble in ammonia, pale-yellow AgBr sparingly soluble, yellow AgI insoluble) distinguishes Cl/Br/I by ammonia solubility ladder. Fluorine needs special tests (etching glass). Beilstein copper-wire green flame screens halogens fast (not fluorine). Layer extraction (CCl4) colours confirm (violet iodine, brown bromine).
NEET Snapshot:
  • Silver precipitates white/yellow; ammonia solubility splits Cl/Br/I.
  • Beilstein green flame prescreens halogens.
Silver halides
PointDetail
AgCl whiteSoluble in ammonia
AgBr pale yellowSparingly soluble
AgI yellowInsoluble
NEET Practice MCQ
1

AgCl precipitate dissolves in ammonia while AgI does not - this separates

Solution: Ammonia-solubility ladder splits silver halides.
Example 1.

Q. Acidified extract gives white precipitate with AgNO3 soluble in ammonia. Identify halogen.

  1. White AgCl precipitate indicates chloride.
  2. Ammonia solubility splits Cl (soluble) from Br/I (less/insoluble).
  3. Chloride confirmed by dissolve test.

Answer: Chloride - white silver salt dissolving in ammonia.

Chapter 8 · Topic 4

Hydroxyl group

Principles Related to Practical ChemistryBiomolecules and Practical ChemistryFunctional-Group DetectionStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Hydroxyl-group tests (alcoholic - ceric ammonium nitrate yellow-to-red, Lucas turbidity rates 3°>2°>1°, oxidation products; phenolic - FeCl3 violet, phthalein dye with phthalic anhydride, Liebermann nitroso) split alcohols from phenols decisively. Iodoform (methyl carbinols) plus periodic acid cleavage (vicinal diols) refine further. -OH presence is necessary but insufficient - class tests follow detection.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Ceric red (alcohols) versus FeCl3 violet (phenols).
  • Lucas rates classify alcohol types.
Remember
  • Phthalein pink proves phenolic OH specifically.
NEET Practice MCQ
1

Phenolic hydroxyl group is detected by reagent giving violet colour, namely

Solution: Phenol-iron complexes diagnose phenolic groups.
Example 1.

Q. An alcohol gives red colour with ceric ammonium nitrate but no turbidity with Lucas cold. Identify class.

  1. Ceric red proves alcoholic OH present.
  2. Lucas silence (cold) means primary alcohol (no carbocation).
  3. Primary alcohol confirmed by the pair.

Answer: Primary alcohol - ceric-positive, Lucas-negative cold.

Chapter 8 · Topic 5

Carbonyl group

Principles Related to Practical ChemistryBiomolecules and Practical ChemistryFunctional-Group DetectionStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Carbonyl-group tests (2,4-DNP orange precipitate for all carbonyls; Tollens silver mirror plus Fehling brick-red for aldehydes only; iodoform yellow for methyl ketones; Schiff magenta restoration for aldehydes) split aldehydes from ketones decisively. Brady reagent (DNP) confirms carbonyl presence; Tollens/Fehling oxidisability separates aldehydes (oxidise) from ketones (resist). Acetaldehyde versus acetone unknowns resolve in two tests.
NEET Snapshot:
  • DNP orange proves carbonyl; Tollens/Fehling prove aldehyde.
  • Iodoform yellow proves methyl carbonyls.
Carbonyl tests
PointDetail
2,4-DNPOrange (all carbonyls)
Tollens/FehlingAldehydes only
IodoformMethyl ketones
NEET Practice MCQ
1

Tollens test distinguishes aldehydes from ketones because only aldehydes

Solution: Aldehydic hydrogen oxidises to acids depositing silver.
Example 1.

Q. An unknown gives orange DNP precipitate but no silver mirror. Identify class with example.

  1. DNP orange proves carbonyl group.
  2. Tollens negative rules out aldehydes (no oxidisable H).
  3. Ketone (e.g., acetone) - carbonyl without aldehydic hydrogen.

Answer: Ketone - DNP-positive, Tollens-negative.

Chapter 8 · Topic 6

Carboxyl group

Principles Related to Practical ChemistryBiomolecules and Practical ChemistryFunctional-Group DetectionStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Carboxyl-group tests (NaHCO3 effervescence CO2 - acids stronger than carbonic; blue litmus reddening; ester formation with fruity smell on warming with alcohol/H2SO4) prove -COOH decisively. Acidity (pH paper, bicarbonate fizz) separates acids from phenols (weaker, no bicarbonate fizz with dilute); esterification confirms plus characterises (fragrant esters identify acids). Dicarboxylic nuances (oxalic calcium precipitation) refine further.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Bicarbonate fizz plus litmus red plus fruity esters prove acids.
  • Stronger-than-carbonic acids release CO2 visibly.
Remember
  • No fizz with bicarbonate rules carboxylic acids out.
NEET Practice MCQ
1

Carboxylic acids effervesce with NaHCO3 because they are

Solution: Stronger acids displace weaker carbonic visibly.
Example 1.

Q. A liquid fizzes with NaHCO3 and smells fruity after warming with ethanol/H2SO4. Identify group.

  1. Fizz proves acid stronger than carbonic (carboxylic).
  2. Fruity ester smell confirms -COOH via esterification.
  3. Carboxylic acid double-confirmed.

Answer: Carboxylic acid - bicarbonate fizz plus ester fragrance.

Chapter 8 · Topic 7

Amino group

Principles Related to Practical ChemistryBiomolecules and Practical ChemistryFunctional-Group DetectionStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Amino-group tests (carbylamine foul isocyanide for primary amines/aliphatic-aromatic; Hinsberg sulphonamide solubility splits 1° soluble/2° insoluble/3° no reaction; nitrous acid: N2 effervescence primary aliphatic, diazonium colours primary aromatic, nitrosamine oils secondary, nothing tertiary; azo-dye coupling confirms aromatic primary) classify plus identify amines completely. Smell, solubility and colours triangulate class and type.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Carbylamine foul (1°), Hinsberg splits (1/2/3°), nitrous colours (aromatic 1°).
  • Azo coupling confirms aromatic primary amines.
Amine tests
PointDetail
CarbylamineFoul smell (1° only)
Hinsberg1° soluble, 2° insoluble, 3° none
HNO2N2 (aliphatic 1°), dyes (aromatic 1°)
NEET Practice MCQ
1

Hinsberg reagent distinguishes amine classes by sulphonamide

Solution: Sulphonamide acidity differences split the three classes.
Example 1.

Q. A foul smell appears mixing unknown with CHCl3/KOH (heat). Identify group.

  1. Carbylamine foul isocyanide proves primary amine.
  2. Only R-NH2 gives the stench (2°/3° silent).
  3. Primary amine confirmed by smell test.

Answer: Primary amine - carbylamine stench diagnostic.

Chapter 8 · Topic 8

Acetanilide

Principles Related to Practical ChemistryBiomolecules and Practical ChemistryCompounds Specifically MentionedStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Acetanilide (N-phenylacetamide: analgesic-antipyretic history, aniline acetylation product, white flakes) tests amide (hydrolysis to aniline plus acetate) plus aromatic amine (post-hydrolysis diazo coupling) characteristics - hydrolysis first, then amine tests. Paracetamol (p-hydroxyacetanilide) succeeded it medically (safer metabolite profile). Purity checked by melting point (114°C sharp); synthesis (aniline plus acetic anhydride) is undergraduate staple.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Amide hydrolysis then aniline tests identify it.
  • Melting point 114°C sharp proves purity.
Remember
  • Paracetamol succeeded acetanilide medically (safer).
NEET Practice MCQ
1

Acetanilide on hydrolysis gives

Solution: Amide cleavage restores amine plus acid components.
Example 1.

Q. White flakes (mp 114C) hydrolyse to give diazo-coupling colours. Identify.

  1. mp 114C suggests acetanilide.
  2. Hydrolysis releases aniline (diazo coupling positive).
  3. Amide hydrolysis plus amine tests identify acetanilide.

Answer: Acetanilide - amide of aniline, mp 114C.

Back to Index
Index / Biomolecules and Practical Chemistry
Chapter 8 · Topic 9

Iodoform

Principles Related to Practical ChemistryBiomolecules and Practical ChemistryCompounds Specifically MentionedStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Iodoform (CHI3 yellow antiseptic-smelling crystals) identifies methyl ketones and methyl carbinols (I2/NaOH haloform: tri-iodination then hydroxide cleavage) - acetophenone positive, benzophenone negative (no methyl). Mechanism (halogenation thrice then C-C cleavage) generalises to chloroform/bromoform with respective halogens. Hospital antiseptic history plus analytical use double its fame.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Yellow precipitate diagnoses CH3CO-/CH3CHOH- groups.
  • Haloform cleavage generalises Cl/Br/I analogues.
Remember
  • Acetophenone positive (methyl); benzophenone negative (phenyl).
NEET Practice MCQ
1

Iodoform test is positive for ethanol because it has group

Solution: Secondary methyl alcohols oxidise in situ then cleave.
Example 1.

Q. Yellow crystals with antiseptic smell form from ethanol + I2/NaOH. Identify product and test meaning.

  1. Yellow CHI3 is iodoform (antiseptic odour).
  2. Positive haloform proves CH3CHOH- or CH3CO- group.
  3. Ethanol qualifies via methyl carbinol structure.

Answer: Iodoform - haloform-positive methyl carbinol.

Chapter 8 · Topic 10

Titrimetric exercises

Topic in Depth

Titrimetric exercises (volumetric analysis: acid-base titrations with phenolphthalein/methyl orange indicators, redox (iodometry, permanganometry), complexometric EDTA hardness, precipitation argentometry) quantify solutions via stoichiometry at equivalence (indicator colour flips). Standard solutions (oxalic acid, Mohr salt primary standards) calibrate; concordant readings (triplicate agreement) validate. Indicator choice (pH-range matching titration curves) decides accuracy.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Titrate to indicator equivalence; compute via stoichiometry.
  • Primary standards calibrate; concordant triplicates validate.
Titration pairs
PointDetail
Strong acid-basePhenolphthalein/methyl orange
RedoxIodometry, permanganometry (self-indicator)
HardnessEDTA complexometry
NEET Practice MCQ
1

Permanganate titrations need no external indicator because KMnO4 is

Solution: Faint permanent pink marks the endpoint directly.
Example 1.

Q. 25 mL oxalic acid solution needs 20 mL 0.1M NaOH (phenolphthalein). Find acid molarity (diprotic).

  1. NaOH moles = 0.1 × 20/1000 = 0.002 = 2 × oxalic moles (diprotic 1:2).
  2. Oxalic moles = 0.001 in 25 mL; molarity = 0.001/0.025 = 0.04 M.
  3. Diprotic stoichiometry halves the titre ratio.

Answer: 0.04 M oxalic acid (1:2 acid-base stoichiometry).

Chapter 8 · Topic 11

Acids

Principles Related to Practical ChemistryBiomolecules and Practical ChemistryOther Practical TopicsStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Acids in titrimetry (HCl, H2SO4 standardised against borax/sodium carbonate; oxalic acid primary standard weighing directly; acetic acid weak needing phenolphthalein) standardise bases - normality (equivalents per litre) simplifies stoichiometry (N1V1=N2V2). Standardisation (titrating against primary standards) precedes unknown analysis. Acid strength (strong fully, weak partially ionised) picks indicators via titration-curve pH jumps.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Standardise against primary standards; titrate with N1V1=N2V2.
  • Oxalic acid weighs directly as primary standard.
Remember
  • Primary standards (oxalic, Mohr salt) need no standardisation.
NEET Practice MCQ
1

Oxalic acid is a primary standard because it is

Solution: High-purity stability allows direct solution-making.
Example 1.

Q. HCl standardised against 0.53 g Na2CO3 (pure) needed 20 mL acid. Find acid molarity. (Na2CO3 = 106)

  1. Moles carbonate = 0.53/106 = 0.005; needs 2× HCl = 0.01 mol.
  2. Molarity = 0.01/0.020 = 0.5 M.
  3. Carbonate consumes two protons per molecule.

Answer: 0.5 M HCl (diprotic carbonate stoichiometry).

Chapter 8 · Topic 12

Bases

Principles Related to Practical ChemistryBiomolecules and Practical ChemistryOther Practical TopicsStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Bases in titrimetry (NaOH standardised against oxalic acid/potassium hydrogen phthalate - hygroscopic, never primary standard; ammonia weak needing methyl orange) standardise acids - carbonate error (absorbed CO2) corrected by boiling. Basicity (NaOH monoacidic, Ca(OH)2 diacidic) sets equivalent weights. Indicator matching (phenolphthalein strong-base endpoints, methyl orange weak-base) decides accuracy.
NEET Snapshot:
  • NaOH standardised (never primary - hygroscopic).
  • Carbonate error boiled out before endpoints.
Remember
  • NaOH pellets absorb water-CO2; standardise, never weigh direct.
NEET Practice MCQ
1

NaOH cannot serve as primary standard because it is

Solution: Water-CO2 uptake changes weighed mass unpredictably.
Example 1.

Q. NaOH pellets left open absorb water and CO2. Why must its solution be standardised?

  1. Weighed mass includes water plus carbonate - true NaOH unknown.
  2. Titrate against oxalic acid/KHP to find real molarity.
  3. Hygroscopic plus CO2-absorbing nature forbids direct weighing.

Answer: Open NaOH misweighs; standardisation finds true strength.

Chapter 8 · Topic 13

Indicators

Principles Related to Practical ChemistryBiomolecules and Practical ChemistryOther Practical TopicsStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Indicators (weak organic acids/bases changing colour across pH ranges: phenolphthalein 8.2-10 colourless-pink, methyl orange 3.1-4.4 red-yellow, litmus 5-8, universal blends rainbow) signal equivalence via structural shifts (quinonoid-benzenoid tautomerism). Choice matches titration jumps (strong-strong either; weak acid needs phenolphthalein; weak base needs methyl orange). Wrong indicators blur endpoints - curve-jump overlap decides.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Colour-change pH ranges must overlap titration jumps.
  • Phenolphthalein basic-side; methyl orange acid-side.
Indicator picks
PointDetail
Strong acid-strong baseEither indicator
Weak acid-strong basePhenolphthalein
Strong acid-weak baseMethyl orange
Weak-weakNo sharp indicator (pH meter)
NEET Practice MCQ
1

Phenolphthalein suits titrations ending on side that is

Solution: Pink appears only above pH 8.2 matching basic endpoints.
Example 1.

Q. Titrating acetic acid with NaOH: phenolphthalein or methyl orange? Why?

  1. Endpoint basic (acetate hydrolyses, pH > 7).
  2. Phenolphthalein (8.2-10) brackets basic endpoints; methyl orange (3-4) misses.
  3. Match indicator range to endpoint pH.

Answer: Phenolphthalein - basic endpoint needs basic-range indicator.

Chapter 8 · Topic 14

Qualitative salt analysis

Principles Related to Practical ChemistryBiomolecules and Practical ChemistryOther Practical TopicsStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Qualitative salt analysis runs cation-anion schemes: preliminary (flame colours: Na golden, K lilac, Ca brick-red; borax-bead colours; charcoal cavity reductions), anion tests (carbonate fizz, sulphide rotten-egg, nitrate brown-ring, halide silver precipitates, sulphate barium white), cation groups (HCl group Ag/Pb/Hg; H2S group Cu/Pb in acid; NH4Cl/NH4OH groups Al/Fe/Cr/Ni/Co/Mn/Zn; carbonate group Ca/Sr/Ba; soluble Na/K/Mg) precipitating stepwise with confirmatory tests closing each ion.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Flame plus bead preliminaries, anion tests, cation group separations.
  • Group reagents precipitate stepwise; confirmatory tests close ions.
Cation groups
PointDetail
HCl diluteAg+, Pb2+, Hg2(2+) chlorides
H2S acidicCu2+, Pb2+ sulphides
NH4Cl/NH4OHAl3+, Fe3+, Cr3+ hydroxides
CarbonateCa2+, Sr2+, Ba2+ carbonates
NEET Practice MCQ
1

Brown-ring test detects anion

Solution: Ferrous-nitrosyl brown ring forms at acid junction.
Example 1.

Q. A salt gives white precipitate with AgNO3 (insoluble in ammonia) plus brown ring test positive. Identify ions.

  1. Ammonia-insoluble white AgX suggests bromide (pale yellow) - recheck colour carefully.
  2. Brown ring proves nitrate alongside.
  3. Combined tests narrow to bromide + nitrate salts (e.g., KBr + KNO3 mixture or single salt logic).

Answer: Bromide (silver test) plus nitrate (brown ring) present.

Chapter 8 · Topic 15

Relevant laboratory experiments

Principles Related to Practical ChemistryBiomolecules and Practical ChemistryOther Practical TopicsStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Relevant laboratory experiments (enthalpy: calorimeter Hess cycles; kinetics: thiosulphate-acid turbidity rates, temperature effects; equilibrium: Fe3+/SCN- colour shifts with concentration-temperature; pH: meter plus indicator measurements; chromatography: ink Rf values; Titrimetry: oxalic-Mohr standardisations) demonstrate physical-chemistry laws hands-on. Lab notebooks (aim, theory, observation tables, calculations, precautions, viva questions) document identically - experiment plus record plus reasoning triples scores.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Calorimetry, kinetics, equilibrium, pH, chromatography, titrimetry core set.
  • Observation tables plus calculations plus precautions document fully.
Remember
  • concordant readings validate; single readings never suffice.
NEET Practice MCQ
1

Calorimeter experiments measure

Solution: Heat exchange at constant pressure equals enthalpy change.
Example 1.

Q. Design an experiment proving temperature raises reaction rates (thiosulphate-acid turbidity).

  1. Fix concentrations, vary temperature baths (20-60C).
  2. Time turbidity appearance (sulphur precipitation) per run.
  3. Plot 1/time vs temperature - rate climbs steeply (Q10 doubling).

Answer: Turbidity timing across temperatures proves rate-temperature link.
